claims.text: The funding opportunity uses a two-stage application process: an outline stage followed by a detailed stage.
The funding is for innovative and original research projects.
Projects can be funded for up to 5 years.
The outline stage of the application process is currently paused.
The outline stage is expected to reopen in autumn 2026.
Detailed applications from invited applicants close on 1 September 2026.
The maximum grant value is £500,000.
Eligible institutions include UK universities and other institutions of higher education in the UK.
UK independent research institutes/organisations are eligible to apply on a trial basis.
The Principal Investigator must be employed by an eligible institution or be an academic with close links to one following retirement.
Contract research post holders are eligible if their appointment duration matches the award span.
Up to three co-applicants from the same or different institutions are allowed, including overseas co-applicants.

Not all subject areas are eligible, specifically excluding medical and clinical research, research influencing policy, research with immediate commercial application, database assembly, advocacy, capacity building, networking, or skills development.
At least 75% of requested resources must fund research staff.
There must be at least one research assistant, overseas research assistant, or PhD student working at least 50% of the time throughout the grant.
Research assistants should have a research degree or equivalent experience.
Overseas research assistants can be employed if the research takes place outside the UK and local personnel are more suitable.
Consultant costs can be included up to a maximum of £5,000 per year, provided they offer specialist expertise not available from co-applicants.
Funding for research technicians who contribute directly to project outputs is allowed.
Tuition fees and maintenance costs for PhD studentships are allowed, set at the UK research council base rate.
PhD students registered overseas are not permitted.
Support for an overseas student registered in the UK is allowable with explicit justification of their skills.
The Trust does not fund partial continuation or completion of independently initiated theses.
Principal Investigators and UK-based co-applicants at UK universities may apply for teaching replacement costs.
A maximum of one year's (33%) teaching replacement per grant is allowed, pro-rata for different grant lengths or part-time contracts.
The replacement for teaching should not be a current research degree student.
Staff replacement costs should normally start at the most junior point of the lecturer scale.
Awards do not cover the salary costs of the applicant or co-applicants based at any university.
During the trial period, applicants/co-applicants at UK independent research institutions with salary-securing contracts may exceptionally apply for a salary contribution.
A maximum of one year's (33%) salary contribution is allowed over a three-year grant, pro-rata for different lengths or part-time contracts.
Associated research costs can be included up to a maximum of 25% of the total budget.
Associated research costs include travel, subsistence, consumables, pool technical services, and computing costs.
Applications for continuation of funding for existing research are not eligible.
Requests for continuation of funding for a research assistant on an existing grant are not normally considered.
Proposals must reflect the applicant's personal vision and demonstrate competence in research design.
The Trust favors applications that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries and involve risk-taking.
Applicants must justify why the Trust is the most appropriate agency for their project.
The Research Project Grants are assessed via a two-stage process: Outline Applications and Detailed Applications.
Detailed applications are only accessible to invited applicants.
Detailed applications are an elaboration of the outline application.
Significant changes to the stated intention, aims, or objectives between stages are not permitted.
The total budget and personnel requested in the detailed application should match the outline, with allowable changes only for salary adjustments to conform to current pay scales.
The earliest possible start date for projects closing on 1 September 2026 is 1 December 2026.

Extensions to the nine-month detailed application deadline can be requested in exceptional circumstances (sudden, unforeseen, outside applicant's control, preventing academic duties for the majority of the period).
Examples of exceptional circumstances for extensions include illness, maternity/paternity/adoption leave, or bereavement.
Workload, fieldwork, teaching duties, or sabbaticals are not considered exceptional circumstances for extensions.
Extensions are usually limited to 3 months and/or the next deadline date.

claims.text: Funds UK institutions to invite an eminent senior professor from overseas.
The professor invited must be eminent and senior.
The professor invited must be from overseas.
The visit duration must be between 3 and 12 months.
The purpose is to bring novel expertise to an underrepresented area of research.
The purpose is to enhance skills and knowledge in an underrepresented area of research.
Applications are invited for a minimum of £10,000.
Applications are invited for a maximum of £150,000.
Applications for less than £10,000 are not eligible.
Applications for more than £150,000 are not eligible.
A Visiting Professorship must last at least 3 months.
Grants between 3 and 6 months must be completed in one visit.
Grants between 6 and 12 months can be spread over two or more visits.
12 months is the maximum duration for a visit.
Applications must be made by a member of academic staff based in a UK university with research degree awarding powers.
Some specialist arts institutions are permitted to apply.
The host academic’s employing institution must agree to administer the grant.
The host institution must provide appropriate facilities for the Visiting Professor.
Visitors who have previously held a Leverhulme Visiting Professorship can only apply if at least 7 years have elapsed since the last one.
The Trust will consider candidates who do not hold a university post in special circumstances.
Collaborative research alone will not be a sufficient justification for a grant.
Priority will be given to new or recent collaborative ventures.
The visitor will provide expertise not otherwise available within the UK research base.
Visiting Professors will be expected to offer a short course of "Leverhulme Lectures".
The Trust will not fund applications for research of which advocacy forms an explicit component.
The Trust does not support research which is aimed principally at an immediate commercial application.
The Trust will not fund applications in which the balance between assembling a data bank or database and the related subsequent research is heavily inclined to the former.
Applications will be considered in all subject areas except studies of disease, illness and disabilities in humans and animals.
Applications will be considered in all subject areas except research intended to inform clinical practice or the development of medical applications.
Visits should be for no less than 3 months.
Visits should be for no more than 12 months.
A Professorship may be spread over a number of visits and over a period of up to 2 years if justified.
Tenures of 6 months or more total duration are eligible to be spread over 2 or more visits.
Tenures of less than 6 months must be completed within one visit.
The award should commence within 15 months of receipt of the offer letter.
The Trust will award a maintenance grant up to a level commensurate with the salary of a professor in the comparable field in the UK.
The maintenance grant is only payable for the period of the visit to the UK.
The Trust will consider funding replacement salary costs for the visitor in their home institution as an alternative to a maintenance grant/salary.
Replacement salary costs should only be requested if more cost-effective than a maintenance grant/salary.
Replacement salary costs are only payable for the period of the visit to the UK.
Visitors may apply for funds for accommodation and utilities in the UK in certain cases.
Travel costs to and from the UK will be met for the visitor and dependant partner.
Travel costs should be based on the lowest reasonable tariff for economy travel.
If two or more visits are made, the Trust will pay for a maximum of two return fares for the visitor and accompanying partner.
Associated costs, if justified by the programme, will also be considered.
Associated costs may include travel within the UK (for the visitor only).
Associated costs may include laboratory consumables.
Associated costs may include technical assistance.
The grant does not cover the costs of items of equipment.
The grant does not cover the costs of non-UK conference attendance and travel.
The grant does not cover departmental costs.
The grant does not cover overheads.
The grant does not cover bench fees.
Personal expenditures on items such as car hire and health insurance are also ineligible.
The Trust does not make awards on a full economic costing basis.
The host institution should provide general support costs such as photocopying.
The host institution should provide general support costs such as inter-library loans.
The host institution should provide general support costs such as routine administrative assistance.
The host institution must meet all overhead and departmental costs.
The host institution must meet costs such as college and bench fees.
The host institution must provide facilities commensurate with existing staff.
The host institution must meet any visa or related costs, such as the NHS Surcharge.
In exceptional circumstances, the Trust may consider funding up to 50% of visa or related costs.
The host institution must manage all necessary arrangements relating to the visitor’s visa and tax requirements.
The host institution must administer the funding in accordance with the approved budget.
The host institution is required to submit a final statement of expenditure within one month of the end of the Professorship.
The visitor and UK host academic are required to submit a brief report within one month of the end of each visit.
The Trust’s support should be acknowledged in any publications arising directly from the visit.
Publications arising from the visit should be listed in the reports.
To make an application, access the Leverhulme Trust Grants Management System.
Applications must be completed by the responsible academic in the UK host institution.
The visiting academic cannot make an application.
The UK host applicant is expected to organise, direct and take academic and organisational responsibility of the Professorship.
Both the proposed Visiting Professor and the UK host institution must give approval by the closing date.
The Trust will report results to applicants within 5 to 6 months of each closing date.

claims.text: The Leverhulme Centenary Research Centre round funds large-scale, outstanding original research.
The research funded by the Leverhulme Centenary Research Centre round aspires to achieve a step-change in scholarship.
The Leverhulme Centenary Research Centre round is expected to open in February 2027.
Outline applications for the Leverhulme Centenary Research Centre round are expected in June 2027.
Previously excluded institutions (Universities of Oxford and Cambridge and Imperial College London) will be eligible to apply in this round.
Up to £10 million is available for this funding round.
Funding is available for up to 10 years.
The Trust aims to encourage new approaches that may establish or reshape a field of study.
The Trust aims to transform our understanding of a significant contemporary topic.
Eligible institutions are universities in the UK registered by the Office for Students and holding their own research degree awarding powers.
A Leverhulme Research Centre may be based at a single university or be a collaboration between multiple institutions.
Collaborative research centres are encouraged.
Each UK university is permitted to submit one application as a principal applicant.
A UK university may act as a partner in multiple proposals led by other universities.
The participation of international institutions is encouraged where relevant.
The Trust has a reputation for encouraging higher-risk research, often fundamental or curiosity-driven ('blue skies').
The research funded is expected to be multi-disciplinary.
The choice of research topic is open, but medical and clinical research are ineligible.
The chosen topic should be sufficiently large-scale to support an ambitious research agenda for up to ten years.
Leverhulme Research Centres should not duplicate existing activity at a comparable scale.
At least 75% of resources must be used for research staff (research assistants, postgraduate students, and replacement teaching).
Replacement teaching is capped at a maximum of 33% for up to three years for key academic staff.
Associated research costs (technical, computing, administrative staff, travel, subsistence, dissemination, consumables) can be included up to a maximum of 25% of the total budget.
Institutions hosting a centre must provide office and workspace and other university support.
The Trust does not make awards on a full economic costing basis.
Increases in costs over the lifetime of the centres must be managed within the awarded funding.
The Trust will not award follow-on funding.
Prospective applicants should follow their university's internal selection process first.
Universities should contact Emily Nisbet at [email protected] with the name and email address of their chosen applicant to gain access to the Grants Management System.
The June 2027 closing date is for the receipt of outline applications.
Invitations for full-stage applications are expected in September.
The deadline for full-stage applications is at the end of the year (December 2027).
Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant based in a UK university who will act as Director.
Details of the proposed wider leadership team should be provided.
Applications are considered via a two-stage process: an outline bid and a detailed proposal.
The outline bid consists of a short form and a five-page description of the proposed centre’s structure and research activity.
The description should include details of the research area, key research questions, and how the centre will contribute.
The description should include the structure of the centre, details of institutions involved, and key staff.
The description should include the justification for the choice of the principal applicant and senior staff.
The description should include an indication of how resources might be used over the centre’s duration.
Those whose outline bids are shortlisted will be invited to submit a detailed proposal and a statement of support from the institution.
Those whose full applications are shortlisted will be invited to interview.
Final decisions are anticipated to be made by the Trust Board at its subsequent board meeting.
The Trust is unable to provide feedback on applications.
